Let \(x_6=x_1\). Since \(0\le x_i\le 1\), each difference \(d_i=|x_i-x_{i+1}|\le 1\), so
\[
d_i^3\le d_i.
\]
Thus
\[
\sum_{i=1}^5 |x_i-x_{i+1}|^3 \le \sum_{i=1}^5 |x_i-x_{i+1}|.
\]

Now prove \(\sum |x_i-x_{i+1}|\le 4\). Let \(\Delta_i=x_{i+1}-x_i\). Then \(\sum_{i=1}^5 \Delta_i=0\). If \(P\) is the sum of the positive \(\Delta_i\), then
\[
\sum_{i=1}^5 |x_i-x_{i+1}|=2P.
\]
Each \(\Delta_i\le 1\). If \(P>2\), then there must be at least \(3\) positive \(\Delta_i\)'s and also at least \(3\) negative \(\Delta_i\)'s, totaling at least \(6\) nonzero increments, impossible for a 5-cycle. Hence \(P\le 2\), so
\[
\sum_{i=1}^5 |x_i-x_{i+1}|\le 4.
\]

Equality is achieved by
\[
x_1=1,\quad x_2=0,\quad x_3=1,\quad x_4=0,\quad x_5=1,
\]
for which the expression is
\[
1^3+1^3+1^3+1^3+0^3=4.
\]

Therefore the maximum value is
\[
\boxed{4}.
\]
